Of course, if the evidence is left in, it's of course subject to the provisional nature of the indication that Your Honour has given. It's, of course, also the nature that the fact that the Prosecution insists on the evidence and the fact that they wish to join it up again perhaps at some later point or some part of -- of a tessera of a mosaic, or what have you. So, in those circumstances, Your Honour, I think the only fair approach in terms of when one looks at 89(D) and the balancing exercise that you have to undertake there in terms of probative value and the need to ensure a fair trial, I would submit the only course for the Trial Chamber to take in these circumstances, having heard the witness, having heard the nature of the evidence, having heard the constant amelioration of his evidence, that Your Honours would exclude the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And in those circumstances, Your Honour, my cross-examination would be entirely limited. But if this is left open, then, Your Honour, then there must be a cross-examination and there must be a cross-examination that is properly investigated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand, Ms. Loukas. I can imagine that the Prosecution would take the position that it's not difficult to make a final determination as to the probative value at this moment, because evidence often does not -- stands alone. On the other hand, it's not very attractive to indicate already that this witness would be recalled for further cross-examination on other evidence which we have not heard yet. May I suggest to the parties whether it would be a solution, so that I just can hear your opinion about that - although it has to be brief, because we are close to 2.00 - that this Chamber will decide to exclude that evidence on the relevant portions. We would then identify that exactly. And then to say that the Prosecution could apply for further admission on the basis of evidence we would hear in a later stage and which would change the importance, the relevance of that evidence, since, as I said before, that, as it stands now, it seems to be of a rather low level. But of course, it might not be fully fair to say that it would remain at that level forever, where the OTP has indicated that, in relation with other evidence, it might be more important. But of course we do not know what that evidence is. We do not know when that evidence will come. Could I just have the response of the parties. What if the Chamber would be inclined to act in this way?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's the inverse of what I was going to propose, that be that Your Honours, given -- your indication of the relatively low probative value at this point, that you leave it in, and if later, as a result of additional evidence, the Defence wishes to recall the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would try to have it the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then of course it would not solve the problem because Ms. Loukas would have to cross-examine on all aspects of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And of course that's the practical problem we are faced with at this moment. Ms. Loukas, could you express any view on --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will express a view. I think a provisional exclusion at this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it would then be exclusion, but not excluding in full a later application to admit it again, or admit it again -- to admit it. And then, of course, not after --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Subject to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- yes, that, of course, is certainly -- there would be first an opportunity to -- I mean, before considering that, of course, you would have an opportunity to have this witness recalled and cross-examine him on the relevant portions as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Well, I think that may be an appropriate course, the course that Your Honour has outlined. Exclusion at this point, subject to a possible application by the Prosecution to reintroduce, in addition with subject to that of course the property opportunity for the Defence to cross-examine in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. That, I would say, goes without saying. Okay. The Chamber will consider the matter. How much time would you need for cross-examination with an exclusion of, well, let's say the two visits, more than two visits, but the visits of two persons mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we take it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, with this evidence excluded, I would have thought I'd come in easily within the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I would have thought between half an hour and an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could the witness please put his earphones on again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber decides that the testimony of this witness in relation to the presence of Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Mandic in places where the witness was detained is excluded. At the same time, not excluding the Office of the Prosecutor for an application to have that inserted at a later stage with all the consequences, that is, further cross-examination on those issues by the Defence. The Chamber also would like to, Ms. Loukas to start the cross-examination tomorrow morning at 9.00. Since I take it that indeed the Defence was prepared for the cross-examination of what appeared in the statements of the witness until yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Other than the mysteriously appearing further information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we'll define more exactly what in the transcript will be excluded, but I think it's clear to the parties. Mr. Music, we'll have to finish for the day. You heard about a decision of the Trial Chamber excluding some of your evidence. Don't be worried about that to the extent that there's anything --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I would like to apologise to Their Honours. But may I just say a word, please? After so many years, I just came to the conclusion now who it was that singled out these 47 men. Can I tell you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Music. At this moment, you cannot add anything to your evidence at this moment. Perhaps if there would be -- tomorrow further questions will be put to you by Ms. Loukas, and perhaps even a few more questions by Ms. Edgerton as well. I just wanted to let you know that it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that it's for reasons of application of appropriate rules of procedure that this decision was taken and it has got nothing to do with you as a person. I just wanted to emphasise this. May I instruct you, Mr. Music, not to speak with anyone, not with -- well, whether it be members of the Defence team, the Prosecution team, or other citizens, or people passing by, not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have been giving until now and you're still about to give expectantly tomorrow morning. We'd like to see you back at 9.00 tomorrow morning. And unless there are any procedural issues, we'll stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, I see that you are at the right side of the glass again, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, yes. In fact, I only came in because I wanted to be an insider rather than an outsider for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're an insider now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But since I came to court, Your Honour, I've had some information which took me by surprise. I understand that Mr. Krajisnik has submitted or sent in to the Trial Chamber a - sorry I now can see Judge El Mahdi as well. Good morning, or good afternoon - a CD containing material in relation to a witness whose evidence was heard recently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not aware at this moment, but I've not been here last week, so it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can short-circuit it this afternoon, given the time. And could I ask this, that I would like to say a little bit more about it but it's perfectly convenient to do it in the morning. If I could ask that the Trial Chamber, by which I include the whole Trial Chamber, if the Trial Chamber would please not look at that CD and not look at that material between now and tomorrow morning and then I can make my submissions in relation to that matter. I think -- I suggest that's the more practical way of dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I verified first of all whether no member of the Trial Chamber has seen the material, apart from looking at CDs is not very interesting, but we have not taken any knowledge of any concept of a CD that supposedly has been sent to us. We'll not do it until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Would that include the offices of the Trial Chamber as well, Your Honour? We would prefer to make the request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I cannot confirm to you that they have not seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I could do is instruct them if they have not seen it, to refrain from any further attention to it, and if they have seen it, not to tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And to keep it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, would be my request. They can't undo what they've done, so thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That will be their instructions for this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll stand adjourned until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of November 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
